text:
sophia: Heads up — we've been getting a cluster of preemptible eviction notices in us-central1 since ~08:12. Notices are shorter than usual and a few active streaming sessions dropped and couldn't reattach, leading to duplicate tokens and tail latency.

mike: saw the P99 spike, roughly +5% on streaming routes. Any idea if provider changed the notice window? :thinking:

sophia: yeah, provider maintenance wave — most eviction notices are ~12–18s now (we usually rely on ~25–30s). Our token handoff assumes >=25s.

jules: that explains the "token mismatch" errors — rotation happening mid-handshake.

anita: paste the logs we saw.

sophia: here:
```
WARN runtime/stream: token rotation mismatch, expected sess-abc123 got sess-def456
ERROR runtime/stream: session proxy failed, requeue rejected (no compatible slot)
```

mike: two failure modes: (1) graceful drain can't finish in short window, (2) token rotation overlaps handshake so acceptor rejects.

jules: what's current fallback? requeue in same pool twice, then route_by_latency which may pick dedicated. But route_by_latency has TTL 3s for streaming so it sometimes bails.

sophia: correct. Also we avoid sending to dedicated unless TTL <3s for cost control.

anita: short-term vs cost: if we move traffic to dedicated during these waves we burn $$ but reduce failed streams. Need quick mitigation + follow-up plan.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: "runtime/ephemeral-token-tolerant-v1" — expected merge window 30m :rocket:

mike: mitigation proposal (fast):
- enable feature-flagged tolerant-handshake (accept token +/-1 rotation id)
- increase requeue_attempts from 2 -> 4 for streaming when flag on
- relax route_by_latency TTL to 6s for routes labeled finance:allow-burst=true

jules: long-term: mixed-capacity reserve — keep 2–4 hot standby spot nodes per region that are claimed during eviction waves. Cheaper than dedicated and preserves token continuity.

anita: runbook draft:
1) toggle emergency feature flag `streaming_handshake_relax` ON
2) bump requeue_attempts
3) enable token-tolerant acceptor
4) spin up 3 hot-standby spot nodes in us-central1
5) open incident ticket and tag finance for cost estimate

sophia: I'm landing a small PR with the tolerant acceptor behind the flag and telemetry for "handshake-mismatch" and "requeue-target" counts.

deploy-bot: PR opened: runtime#5427 by sophia — tests included, feature flag gated :white_check_mark:

mike: I'll be ready to flip the flag if the second wave starts. Can finance eyeball cost of 10% dedicated fallback vs 3 standby spots for a 10m window?

anita: tagging @finance-team in the incident ticket. Initial quick calc: avg concurrent streams ~1.2k; 10% -> 120 sessions. If those go to dedicated at 0.2 GPU share each that's ~24 GPU-minutes per minute -> ~0.4 GPU-hours for 10m. Will confirm $ impact.

jules: I'll create a follow-up in infra-ops to debate preemptible SLOs vs latency SLOs and propose thresholding logic (e.g., if eviction-rate > X over 5m, scale standby).

sophia: adding monitoring panels: handshake-mismatch-rate, requeue-success-rate, streaming P99, standby-claim-rate, dedicated-fallback-usage.

mike: temporary mitigation seems good. If tolerance reduces failed reattach we avoid many expensive dedicated fallbacks.

anita: agree. Also let's keep the tolerant acceptor tightly scoped to streaming sessions and behind the flag so we can roll back quickly.

sophia: deploying to staging now, will watch telemetry and report back in this thread. Thanks — i'll open the incident ticket and add cost check once finance responds. :ear:
